routes.notes: form username+password; returns access_token (JWT) on success
form email; INTERNAL-marked but reachable; returns the reset token in the JSON response
form username+token+new_password; sets a new password if the reset token matches
ADMIN-marked; requires Bearer token; echoes request headers/form/body
ADMIN-marked; requires Bearer token; form file_name; returns base64 file content from /cornhub

observations: POST /auth/forgot_password with a known email returns {"token": ...} directly in the response body, so the reset token does not need to be guessed.
POST /auth/update_password with that token resets the target account's password (e.g. admin), enabling full account takeover.
After takeover, POST /auth/login returns a valid Bearer JWT accepted by the admin-only endpoints.
POST /process/documents applies a filter() that rejects '..' and leading '/', but then calls os.path.expandvars() on the file name AFTER the filter.

A file_name of ${HOME}/flag_1.txt passes the filter (no '..' or leading '/'), expands to an absolute path /home/appuser/flag_1.txt, and os.path.join discards the /cornhub base directory, yielding arbitrary file read outside the intended document directory.
